- A hash chain / blockchain-like structure, but with Merkle roots per entry
- Each entry i contains: H(prev_root || payload_i) or more precisely the entry commits to the previous state root
- Tamper evidence: any modification to any historical entry breaks the chain of commitments

- Each entry e_i = (i, r_{i-1}, p_i, m_i, σ_i) where:

**Design A: Recursive hash chain (each root commits to everything)**

r_i = H(r_{i-1} || H(e_i))

This is O(1) per append but proofs are O(n) — you need to replay the whole chain to prove inclusion of e_j at height n. Actually with this structure, proving that e_j is included requires showing the chain from j to n, which is O(n - j). For full audit from genesis it's O(n).

So tampering with any old entry changes its hash, which changes some intermediate node, which changes r_k for all k ≥ position, breaking consistency checks against later signed roots.
